label: def:q-flat-connection
title: $q$-Flat connection
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe and let \mathcal{V} be a G_q-equivariant object in \mathbf{C} over the brane curve X. A q-flat connection on \mathcal{V} is a q-connection \nabla_q \colon \mathcal{V} \to \Omega^1_q \otimes \mathcal{V} (categorical q-connection) whose total curvature \nabla_q^2 equals the intrinsic q-curvature determined by d_q^2:

  \nabla_q^2 = (q - 1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}.

Here, \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}} \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{V}) \otimes \Omega^2_q is the intrinsic q-curvature, defined as the image of the obstruction class \kappa_0 under the Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg map (Kummer filtration):

  \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}
  = 
  \mathrm{HKR}^{-1}(\kappa_0)
   \in 
  HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}).

Concretely, in the classical limit q \to 1, the prefactor (q - 1) vanishes, so the intrinsic term drops out and q-flatness reduces to ordinary flatness (\nabla_q^2 = 0); the residual curvature is present only when q \neq 1.

In general, a q-connection has total curvature

  \nabla_q^2 = (q - 1)\mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{intr}}
  + \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}},

where \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}} is the connection-dependent curvature — the contribution from the connection form itself. A q-connection is q-flat when \mathcal{F}_q^{\mathrm{conn}} = 0: all curvature is intrinsic, arising solely from the d_q^2 \neq 0 obstruction (non-vanishing of d_q^2).

The category of q-flat connections on X with structure group G_q is equivalent to the category of q-local systems \mathrm{LocSys}_{G_q}(X) (q-local system).
